lede: The biggest item this week is Tuesday's Telluride Town Council meeting, where the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code comes up for its third and final reading — pass it and the Land Use Code changes for good, reshaping what property owners can do with landscaping and historic structures. Before that, Wednesday's San Miguel County BOCC holds public hearings on three Land Use Code amendments, including a redefinition of 'Qualified Owner' in affordable housing rules and a wildfire areas update, and the Telluride Housing Authority Subcommittee weighs in on a deed-restriction variance for a Telluride homeowner facing a $47,000 roof bill. Jazz Fest kicks off Friday to round out the week.

notable.stake: Public hearings on three county Land Use Code changes, including affordable housing ownership rules.
Vote on whether a deed-restricted homeowner can exceed capital improvement limits for a new roof.
Architecture and conditional-use permit reviews for three new multifamily projects in Mountain Village.
Third and final reading of Wildfire Resiliency Code — permanent Land Use Code change if approved.
